theorems.name: Theorem W (whole-prefix shift-and-subtract cutoff, general two-prime form)
theorems.statement: Fix primes p (denominator) and l (numerator). Take a path of affine steps y -> (l^a y + c)/p^e with values whose denominators are prime to p, and N events (c != 0). Assume: (H1) labels lie in a finite set; (H2) |tau_i| <= C at events (non-descent); (H3) N, max|A_j| <= C(E+1); (H4) the events split into at most J pieces with bounded internal geometry, each piece being either hereditarily shift-invariant (for every subinterval I' and delta there is a shift q <= delta|I'| with fixed exponent increment, k_E >= 1, |log gamma| <= C, and at most M(delta) exceptions) or periodic of bounded period. Arbitrary jumps are allowed between pieces. Then for every eta > 0 and |y_0| >= y_*(eta, p, l, C, J, M, labels), ineffective: total divisions E <= (1+eta) log_p|y_0|. The coefficient 1 is sharp.

theorems.name: Lemma R (rotation schedules satisfy (H4))
theorems.statement: Block words C^{k_i} X_{lambda_i} whose exits all have the same slope mu < 1, with K_i = c + floor(kappa i + t) + w(phi_i), labels Lambda(phi_i), kappa = log(1/mu)/log(lambda_C), and w, Lambda step functions with at most J arcs and |w| <= B, are shift pieces with M(delta) = 2(2J+1)(1/delta+2), gamma in [1/lambda_C, lambda_C], and bounded geometry. Periodic exit patterns, including unequal slopes, and ramps are geometric pieces.

theorems.name: Theorem P (type (c) implies positive-dimension non-descending set) and converse
theorems.statement: In a unit-multiplier p-adic table map (standing hypothesis), if some SCC of G_K is of type (c) there are closed walks U != V of equal length at a node of the expanding cycle such that every word of {U,V}^* has all prefix slopes > 1. Hence dim_H of the set of points with all prefix slopes >= 1 is at least s > 0, where p^{-s e_U} + p^{-s e_V} = 1, and every interval of p^{K+E} integers contains at least 2^{floor(E/max e)} slope-non-descending starts. Conversely, with no type-(c) SCC that set is countable. So dim > 0 iff type (c).

theorems.name: Lemma Q and Corollary P1 (cylinder-level rigidity impossible)
theorems.statement: Rigid families of Theorem W/Lemma R with fixed (J,B) contain at most (cE)^{c'J} words with at most E divisions. Hence in every type-(c) unit-multiplier system the rigid fraction of non-descending words is at most poly(E)·2^{-E/max(e_U,e_V)} -> 0. No type-(c) table, existing or designed, has every long non-descending cylinder word rigid; without type (c), Theorem H already settles the system.

theorems.name: Proposition B (blocked mixed-base system mb_s3_27)
theorems.statement: Off the class 26 mod 27 the map is Terras 3x+1 with T(n) mod 27 = f(n mod 27, n mod 2), so never-blocked paths are Terras words with a Z/27 automaton and are realized by CRT classes. With C = 110 (the cycle -5,-7,-10, states 22,20,17), W = 010, U = C^25 W^3 and V = C^28 (length 84), every word in {U,V}^* avoids 26 and has all prefix slopes > 1. The non-descending set therefore has 2-adic dimension >= 1/84 per 27-class, and its survivors are not rigid.

theorems.statement: Let T be a table map satisfying (P), and fix a level K. theorems.statement: For any single-prime table map with a certified negative-drift moment certificate (s, gamma, w) (signed constants allowed), the number V(X) of updates with value <= X on a non-eventually-periodic orbit satisfies V(X) <= W p^theta X^theta + s*ceil(log_p X)*E, theta = 1 - gamma, W = sum w/w_min, E = the orbit's total log error (finite by a crude bound with window length kappa log_p X). Hence V(X) <= X^{theta*+o(1)}, theta* the optimal moment exponent. Under (P),(R), raw visits <= R*V(X/c_raw).

theorems.name: Theorem 3 (multiplier bound and dichotomy)
theorems.statement: If all values of a non-periodic orbit are >= p^k0, then E <= E*(k0) = g' W p^theta S1/(1 - g' s S2) (explicit), so 1 <= x_t/(x_0 P_t) < e^{E*} (constants >= 0) or two-sided in the signed case; P_t -> infinity on every non-periodic orbit, P_t -> 0 on eventually periodic ones when constants are >= 0 (fails for 3x-1: cycle multipliers 3/2, 9/8, 2187/2048).

theorems.name: Theorem 4 (chain theorem, general)
theorems.statement: Under (N),(P),(R), on an escaping orbit the successive last minimisers of the update multiplier give starts x_i in N^mult (subset of the never-dropping set), links with ratio in (1, rho], rho = largest edge slope, exact expansion count a = floor(e log(1/kappa)/log rho)+1 for two-slope maps, strip x_{i+1} = r x_i + C_i with explicit bounds, forced residue classes (first k* edges expand), and at least A(B) = max{k: rho^k < 2^B} selected starts in every B consecutive late octaves. Signed version for m3_b, 3x-1.

theorems.name: Proposition 5.1 (gap statement)
theorems.statement: With constants >= 0 and unit multipliers: N^mult (starts whose raw multiplier never drops below 1) is empty iff every positive orbit is eventually periodic; if nonempty it has >= A(B) members in every late B-octave window (so >= log X/log rho - O(1) below X), and it is empty on every verified range. Hence the window criterion for N^mult itself is a restatement of GLOBAL; the non-trivial targets are finite-depth survivor sets.

theorems.name: Theorem W (whole-prefix S-unit cutoff, general two-prime affine paths)
